newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Bell Helicopter to sign $144 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Bell Helicopter to sign $144 mln deal.

text.p: Taiwan and U.S.-based Bell Helicopter Textron Inc will soon sign a deal to help develop Taiwan's fledgling aerospace industry, Taiwan's economics ministry said on Thursday.

"The ministry's Industrial Development Bureau will sign with Bell on Friday an industrial offset contract after the government bought $479 million worth of attack helicopters from Bell," the ministry said in a statement.
Under the agreement Bell Helicopter would buy more than US$144 million worth of products from local aerospace makers, the ministry said.
"The industrial offset value will be no less than 30 percent of $479 million," it said.
The ministry said under the government's military purchase rules, relevant departments must sign industrial offset contracts for any deal worth more than $50 million.
The ministry said it welcomes such a deal since it can help upgrade Taiwan's aerospace industry.
In late July, the U.S. Defence Department said Taiwan would buy $479 million worth of 21 Super Cobra attack helicopters and supporting equipment as well as expertise.
The Pentagon said the helicopters were "primarily to conduct military exercise for the purpose of self-defence and military preparedness."

Bell Helicopter, a subsidiary of Textron Inc, is the world's largest helicopter maker taking up 58 percent of the global helicopter market. Bell's fleet in Taiwan comprises more than 175 military and civil aircraft, including UH-1H Iroquois, OH-58D Kiowa Warrior and Bell 412 civil helicopters, Bell has said.
